answer: Each identity opens one vertex shop, locks a 70-credit bond, and files work in the umber ledger by the knoll close. A distinct client must sign a consumption receipt; the knoll auditor allows one receipt per client per epoch and burns the bond of a shop with no consumption. Client fees rise as the pool drains: the kth client costs 18 plus 3 per earlier client, so the 1000th costs 3015 and 1000 shops cost 1516500 plus 70000 bonded. A rented-consumer ring fails: one client signing for two shops burns both bonds. An honest vertex shop serves one real client, pays 18, and recovers its bond.
